title: Loop the Loopies!
relevance_reason: Large-scale looped MoE LMs (20B-A2B, 6B-A0.6B) pre-trained from scratch with per-layer recurrence and compute-matched baselines.
one_sentence: Introduces layer-loop recurrence (each MoE layer applied twice before the next) plus a wall-clock-matched width/depth recipe; Loopie-20B-A2B overtakes a reproduced Qwen3-like 30B-A3B after about 600B tokens at matched step time.
key_contributions: Layer-loop (per-layer repeat, L1 L1 L2 L2 ...) vs model-loop (whole-stack, as in Ouro/Huginn), with a controlled ablation favoring layer-loop on MoE backbones.
Loopie Recipe: halve stored layers, loop each twice, spend activation-memory headroom on doubled microbatch and wider/deeper stored model, select config by measured optimizer-step time.
Large-scale post-training (supervised pre-training on 2T tokens + math RL) producing Loopie Thinking models.

title: Solve the Loop: Attractor Models for Language and Reasoning
relevance_reason: Weight-tied refinement module solved to a fixed point with implicit gradients; LM pretraining up to 770M vs parameter-matched Transformer and looped Parcae.
one_sentence: A non-recurrent backbone proposes an output embedding; a small weight-tied attractor module refines it to a fixed point (Anderson solver, one-step implicit gradient), beating parameter-matched Transformers and Parcae at 140M-770M with constant training memory.
key_contributions: Fixed point placed in tied output-embedding space, warm-started from the backbone proposal (not zero/noise), with persistent additive proposal injection.
One-step implicit-gradient training: constant memory in iterations and 25-31% fewer training FLOPs than Parcae at the same Tmax.
Equilibrium internalization: after training, decoding the backbone proposal with zero solver steps is near the converged quality.

title: Scaling up Test-Time Compute with Latent Reasoning: A Recurrent Depth Approach
relevance_reason: Canonical prelude-core-coda recurrent-depth LM (3.5B, 800B tokens) with randomized loop counts and test-time depth scaling.
one_sentence: Pretrains a 3.5B prelude (2) / recurrent core (4) / coda (2) LM on 800B tokens with random-noise initial state, per-step concatenation injection and log-normal-Poisson loop counts; accuracy improves with test-time iterations up to about 32-64.
key_contributions: Template P -> R^r (with injection of e each step, s0 random) -> C, with sandwich normalization and a concatenation adapter, trained with r sampled from a heavy-tailed log-normal Poisson and truncated backprop through the last 8 iterations.

title: MoEUT: Mixture-of-Experts Universal Transformers
relevance_reason: Shared-layer (UT) language model with MoE FFN and MoE attention, layer grouping and peri-layernorm; parameter- and MAC-matched against dense Transformers up to about 1B.
one_sentence: MoEUT repeats a group of G (2-4) non-shared fine-grained-MoE layers (sigma-MoE FFN + SwitchHead attention) about 8-9 times with peri-layernorm; it slightly beats parameter-matched dense Transformers on C4 perplexity with fewer MACs, up to 1B parameters.
key_contributions: Solves the UT parameter-compute ratio problem by making the shared layers MoE in both FFN and attention, so parameters can be matched to a dense model without proportional compute.
Layer grouping: recurrently stack a group of G non-shared layers (ABAB...), G=2 optimal at 244M; AABB ordering is almost as bad as no grouping.
Peri-layernorm: no layernorm on the main residual path, only before linear layers feeding sigmoid/softmax, addressing residual-norm growth in shared layers.

title: Adaptive Computation Time for Recurrent Neural Networks
relevance_reason: Origin of learned halting: a weight-shared state transition iterated a variable, learned number of times per input with a ponder cost; adopted by Universal Transformers and later looped LMs.
one_sentence: Adds a sigmoidal halting unit to an RNN so it performs a learned, input-dependent number of shared-weight state updates per input step, combined by a mean-field halting distribution and regularized by a ponder cost; large gains on synthetic tasks, little on character LM.

title: The Topological Trouble With Transformers
relevance_reason: Position paper arguing feedforward depth (including depth recurrence) cannot do unbounded state tracking; offers a taxonomy of recurrent transformers by recurrence axis and token-to-step ratio.
one_sentence: Argues transformers push evolving state deeper with each input step and eventually exhaust depth; depth recurrence alone does not fix this, so step-wise (cross-token) recurrence or coarse-grained recurrence is needed; gives a recurrence-axis x tokens-per-step taxonomy.
key_contributions: Topological argument: in a feedforward transformer, state representations shift upward in the layer stack with each new token, so tracking is limited by depth.
Taxonomy of recurrent transformers by recurrence axis (depth, step, both) and ratio of input tokens per recurrence step (>1, =1, <1).
Research directions: enhanced state-space models and coarse-grained recurrence.

claims.claim: Feedforward transformers exhaust their depth on state tracking because state representations move deeper with each input step.
claims.evidence_quote: feedforward models push evolving state representations deeper into their layer stack with each new input step, rendering information inaccessible in shallow layers and ultimately exhausting the model’s depth.

claims.claim: Depth recurrence (looped transformers) does not by itself remove the upward drift of state across input steps.
claims.evidence_quote: state representation still shifts upward due to the parallel propagation of activation across steps t, regardless of how deep the transformer is made to be with recurrent depth (Figure 1b).

claims.claim: Proposes a two-dimensional taxonomy: recurrence axis and input tokens per recurrence step.
claims.evidence_quote: We characterize architectures along two dimensions: recurrence axis and input tokens per recurrence step. The axis can be depth alone (Figures 5b,c,d), in step alone (Figure 7), and in both depth and step (Figure 6).

limitations: No experiments; argument is schematic; examples of state-tracking failures are anecdotal model traces.
survey_notes: Useful for the design-space section as an external taxonomy: places looped transformers / UT / RINS in the 'depth axis, ratio > 1' cell, distinct from step-axis recurrence (linear attention, Mamba) and both-axis models (continuous thought). Its claim that depth recurrence cannot fix state tracking across tokens is a theoretical caution against over-claiming for LoopLMs; contrast with works that report state-tracking gains from looping (theory group papers).

title: Looping Beyond Twice: A Scalable Recipe for Looped Mixture-of-Experts
relevance_reason: Whole-stack looped MoE LM with per-loop routers, residual scaling, gated embedding re-injection and a looping residual; near-iso-FLOP and non-iso-FLOP loop sweeps 100M-1.7B.
one_sentence: Diagnoses curse-of-depth variance growth and expert-selection collapse in looped MoE; LOOM fixes them with residual scaling, convex embedding re-injection, loop-specific routers and an EMA looping residual, scaling to 9-12 loops and winning at near-iso-FLOP with 5 loops at 700M.
key_contributions: Two failure modes of deep looped MoE: residual variance growth across loops and routers choosing nearly the same experts each loop.

Recipe: residual branch scale gamma = lambda / (H sqrt(M)), re-injection h0^t = (1 - g_t) h^{t-1} + g_t x with g_t = lambda / (t sqrt(M)), per-loop routers over shared experts, EMA looping residual, segmented backprop (K=3).

title: DiscoLoop: Looping Discrete Embeddings and Continuous Hidden States for Multi-hop Reasoning
relevance_reason: Whole-stack looped transformer whose inter-loop state adds a gated soft decode-then-encode embedding channel; symbolic two-hop reasoning and 440M pretraining vs vanilla loop and PonderLM.
one_sentence: Finds that vanilla looped transformers decode the bridge entity after loop 1 but pass a hidden state misaligned with its token embedding; DiscoLoop adds a gated soft decoded-embedding channel between loops, fixing two-hop OOD generalization and slightly improving 440M pretraining.
key_contributions: Mechanistic diagnosis: looping fixes depth-local fact storage but leaves a representation mismatch between the post-loop hidden state and the clean bridge-token embedding; a training-free realignment nearly closes the gap.

DiscoLoop recurrence: H~(k+1) = H(k+1) + alpha(k) ⊙ RMSNorm(Phi(H(k+1))), where Phi is a temperature-softmax over LM-head logits mapped back through the embedding matrix; alpha is fixed or a d+1-parameter learned gate.
Gains on symbolic and synthetic-language two-hop tasks (ID and OOD) and on 440M/20B-token pretraining vs vanilla loop and PonderLM.

title: Sparse Growing Transformer: Training-Time Sparse Depth Allocation via Progressive Attention Looping
relevance_reason: Component-level looping of selected high-entropy attention heads, grown deep-to-shallow during pretraining; compared with block-level looping at matched params and tokens.
one_sentence: SGT progressively adds recurrence during training only to high-entropy attention heads, starting from deeper layers and growing toward shallower ones; it matches or beats static block looping while adding 1-3% instead of 16-20% training FLOPs.
key_contributions: Analysis: high-entropy heads act as semantic integration hubs; layers mature deep-to-shallow during training.
Training-time structural sparsity: entropy-guided, staged growth of attention-head looping (loop depth up to Kmax per selected layer), FFN applied once.
Theory that concentrating recurrence on high-entropy components speeds convergence; experiments at 573M and 1.2B with LLaMA-style models.

title: A Dual-Path Architecture for Scaling Compute and Capacity in LLMs
relevance_reason: Hybrid layer with a per-layer looped (K-times shared) sublayer in parallel with a wide once-applied sublayer, gated per token; iso-FLOP comparisons against pure-loop and pure-wide controls.
one_sentence: Each block runs a deep sublayer looped K times with shared weights in parallel with a wider once-applied sublayer, combined by dense per-token gates; at two iso-FLOP budgets the best mix beats both pure-loop and pure-wide controls with fewer parameters than pure-wide.

Deep path output is a learned halting-style weighted combination of all intermediate loop states (router on state and normalized step index).
Interpretable gates: function words and lexical content go wide; punctuation, symbols and arithmetic tokens go deep.

title: SCORE: Replacing Layer Stacking with Contractive Recurrent Depth
relevance_reason: Replaces stacked layers with one shared block iterated under a relaxed (Euler/Krasnoselskii-Mann) contractive update; LM evidence only at nanoGPT/Shakespeare scale.
one_sentence: SCORE iterates a single shared block with the relaxed update h_{t+1} = (1 - dt) h_t + dt F(h_t) (dt = 0.5 or 1/K), improving convergence on GNNs (ESOL), MLPs and small nanoGPT models with fewer parameters.
key_contributions: Contractive residual recurrence as an explicit Euler step of dh/dt = F(h) - h, i.e. a static residual gate.
Comparison of Euler, Heun, Midpoint and RK4 updates; Euler gives the best cost/performance trade-off.
Applies the same recurrence to GNNs, dense nets and Transformers.

title: LSTM-UT and Recurrent-Depth Transformers on Cellular Automata
relevance_reason: Compares state-carrying mechanisms in recurrent-depth transformers (current state only, CoTFormer expanding cache, LSTM-gated cell) on synthetic cellular-automaton tasks; no LM pretraining.

Interventions show CoTFormer's depth failure comes from the interaction of state and retained history, and that it does not select the requested cached block in delayed recall.
LSTM-UT as a bounded gated-memory alternative.

Component ablation: untying attention matters an order of magnitude more than untying routers; a 2+2 untied prelude/coda is the single largest gain; MoEUT-style full tying is clearly worse.
Heterogeneous width expansion: reinvest saved parameters into more experts in tied layers, beating the untied baseline at iso-parameters.

Untied attention per pass (experts and routers shared), adding parameters but no compute; yields more balanced and confident routing.
Design guidance: looping and widening expert layers amplify each other; routing confidence tracks healthy expert use better than load balance; use more experts per layer and more passes.

title: LoopMoE: Unifying Iterative Computation with Mixture-of-Experts for Language Modeling
relevance_reason: Sandwich looped MoE LM with iteration- and token-conditioned adaptive norm, compared to a vanilla MoE at identical total params, per-token FLOPs and active attention/FFN ratio at 3B and 9B.
one_sentence: LoopMoE (2 prefix + 2-layer MoE block x4 + 2 suffix) uses IterAdaLN (affine norm params from iteration index and token state) and rebalances MLA ranks vs expert sizes so it can be matched to a vanilla MoE in total params, per-token FLOPs and active ratio; gains grow from about 1 point (3B) to about 3 points (9B).
key_contributions: IterAdaLN: replaces RMSNorm with adaptive norm conditioned jointly on a sinusoidal iteration embedding and the per-token hidden state, breaking weight-sharing symmetry.
Capacity balancing: adjust MLA Q/KV LoRA ranks and expert hidden size, then expert count, to restore the attention-to-FFN active ratio and total parameters of a well-tuned vanilla MoE.
Strictly matched head-to-head evaluation vs vanilla MoE (same total params, per-token FLOPs, data order) at 3B/200B tokens and 9B/300B tokens.

key_contributions: Top-down energy-based derivation: symmetric attention and feedforward with RMS normalization as iterative optimization steps with shared parameters.
Recurrent-depth instantiation with one set of shared parameters; variants (linear attention, gated FF) and learnable step sizes.
Depth-wise LoRA adapters per iteration as a relaxed-sharing scaling extension.

Zero-Token mechanism: per-layer/per-cycle token with learnable key and all-zero value prepended in attention, distinguishing cycles and allowing skip-like behavior.
Attention to the zero token as an early-exit signal; FFN gating; applicable to fine-tuning GPT-2/OPT.

title: Write Back the $Δ$: Revisiting the Same Tokens with Fresh Representations
relevance_reason: Feedback of deeper residual increments to earlier layers (a second synchronous pass = depth recurrence; streaming variant feeds subsequent tokens).
